entries.name: ::after
entries.summary: In CSS, ::after creates a pseudo-element that is the last child of the selected element. It is often used to add cosmetic content to an element with the content property. It is inline by default.

entries.name: ::backdrop
entries.summary: The ::backdrop CSS pseudo-element is a box the size of the viewport, which is rendered immediately beneath any element being presented in the top layer.

entries.name: ::before
entries.summary: In CSS, ::before creates a pseudo-element that is the first child of the selected element. It is often used to add cosmetic content to an element with the content property. It is inline by default.

entries.name: ::checkmark
entries.summary: The ::checkmark CSS pseudo-element targets the checkmark placed inside the currently-selected <option> element of a customizable select element. It can be used to provide a visual indication of which option is selected.

entries.name: ::column
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: ::cue
entries.summary: The ::cue CSS pseudo-element matches WebVTT cues within a selected element. This can be used to style captions and other cues in media with VTT tracks.

entries.name: ::details-content
entries.summary: The ::details-content CSS pseudo-element represents the expandable/collapsible contents of a <details> element.

entries.name: ::file-selector-button
entries.summary: The ::file-selector-button CSS pseudo-element represents the button of an <input> of type="file".

entries.name: ::first-letter
entries.summary: The ::first-letter CSS pseudo-element applies styles to the first letter of the first line of a block container, but only when not preceded by other content (such as images or inline tables).

entries.name: ::first-line
entries.summary: The ::first-line CSS pseudo-element applies styles to the first line of a block container.

entries.name: ::grammar-error
entries.summary: The ::grammar-error CSS pseudo-element represents a text segment which the user agent has flagged as grammatically incorrect.

entries.name: ::highlight()
entries.summary: The ::highlight() CSS pseudo-element applies styles to a custom highlight.

entries.name: ::marker
entries.summary: The ::marker CSS pseudo-element selects the marker box of a list item, which typically contains a bullet or number.

entries.name: ::part()
entries.summary: The ::part CSS pseudo-element represents any element within a shadow tree that has a matching part attribute.

entries.name: ::picker-icon
entries.summary: The ::picker-icon CSS pseudo-element targets the picker icon inside form controls that have an icon associated with them.

entries.name: ::picker()
entries.summary: The ::picker() CSS pseudo-element targets the picker part of an element, for example the drop-down picker of a customizable select element.

entries.name: ::placeholder
entries.summary: The ::placeholder CSS pseudo-element represents the placeholder text in an <input> or <textarea> element.

entries.name: ::scroll-button()
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: ::scroll-marker
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: ::scroll-marker-group
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: ::search-text
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: ::selection
entries.summary: The ::selection CSS pseudo-element applies styles to the part of a document that has been highlighted by the user (such as clicking and dragging the mouse across text).

entries.name: ::slotted()
entries.summary: The ::slotted() CSS pseudo-element represents any element that has been placed into a slot inside an HTML template (see Using templates and slots for more information).

entries.name: ::spelling-error
entries.summary: The ::spelling-error CSS pseudo-element represents a text segment which the user agent has flagged as incorrectly spelled.

entries.name: ::target-text
entries.summary: The ::target-text CSS pseudo-element represents the text that has been scrolled to if the browser supports text fragments. It allows authors to choose how to highlight that section of text.

entries.name: ::view-transition
entries.summary: The ::view-transition CSS pseudo-element represents the root of the view transitions overlay, which contains all view transition snapshot groups and sits over the top of all other page content.

entries.name: ::view-transition-group()
entries.summary: The ::view-transition-group() CSS pseudo-element represents a single view transition snapshot group.

entries.name: ::view-transition-image-pair()
entries.summary: The ::view-transition-image-pair() CSS pseudo-element represents a container for a view transition's "old" and "new" view states — before and after the transition.

entries.name: ::view-transition-new()
entries.summary: The ::view-transition-new() CSS pseudo-element represents the "new" view state of a view transition — a snapshot live representation of the state after the transition.

entries.name: ::view-transition-old()
entries.summary: The ::view-transition-old() CSS pseudo-element represents the "old" view state of a view transition — a static snapshot of the old view, before the transition.

entries.name: :active
entries.summary: The :active CSS pseudo-class represents an element (such as a button) that is being activated by the user. When using a mouse, "activation" typically starts when the user presses down the primary mouse button.

entries.name: :active-view-transition
entries.summary: The :active-view-transition CSS pseudo-class matches the root element of a document when a view transition is in progress (active) and stops matching once the transition has completed.

entries.name: :active-view-transition-type()
entries.summary: The functional :active-view-transition-type() CSS pseudo-class matches elements when a view transition with one or more specific types is in progress (is active) and stops matching once the view transition has completed.

entries.name: :any-link
entries.summary: The :any-link CSS pseudo-class selector represents an element that acts as the source anchor of a hyperlink, independent of whether it has been visited.

entries.name: :autofill
entries.summary: The :autofill CSS pseudo-class matches when an <input> element has its value autofilled by the browser. The class stops matching if the user edits the field.

entries.name: :blank
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :buffering
entries.summary: The :buffering CSS pseudo-class selector represents an element that is playable, such as <audio> or <video>, when the playable element is buffering a media resource.

entries.name: :checked
entries.summary: The :checked CSS pseudo-class selector represents any radio (<input type="radio">), checkbox (<input type="checkbox">), or option (<option> in a <select> element) that is checked or toggled to an on state.

entries.name: :current
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :default
entries.summary: The :default CSS pseudo-class selects form elements that are the default in a group of related elements.

entries.name: :defined
entries.summary: The :defined CSS pseudo-class represents any element that has been defined.

entries.name: :dir()
entries.summary: The :dir() CSS pseudo-class matches elements based on the directionality of the text contained in them.

entries.name: :disabled
entries.summary: The :disabled CSS pseudo-class represents any disabled element. An element is disabled if it can't be activated (selected, clicked on, typed into, etc.) or accept focus.

entries.name: :empty
entries.summary: The :empty CSS pseudo-class represents any element that has no children. Children can be either element nodes or text (including whitespace).

entries.name: :enabled
entries.summary: The :enabled CSS pseudo-class represents any enabled element. An element is enabled if it can be activated (selected, clicked on, typed into, etc.) or accept focus.

entries.name: :first
entries.summary: The :first CSS pseudo-class, used with the @page at-rule, represents the first page of a printed document. (See :first-child for general first element of a node.)

entries.name: :first-child
entries.summary: The :first-child CSS pseudo-class represents the first element among a group of sibling elements.

entries.name: :first-of-type
entries.summary: The :first-of-type CSS pseudo-class represents the first element of its type (tag name) among a group of sibling elements.

entries.name: :focus
entries.summary: The :focus CSS pseudo-class represents an element (such as a form input) that has received focus. It is generally triggered when the user clicks or taps on an element or selects it with the keyboard's Tab key.

entries.name: :focus-visible
entries.summary: The :focus-visible pseudo-class applies while an element matches the :focus pseudo-class and the UA (User Agent) determines via heuristics that the focus should be made evident on the element.

entries.name: :focus-within
entries.summary: The :focus-within CSS pseudo-class matches an element if the element or any of its descendants are focused.

entries.name: :fullscreen
entries.summary: The :fullscreen CSS pseudo-class matches every element that is currently in fullscreen mode. If multiple elements have been put into fullscreen mode, this selects them all.

entries.name: :future
entries.summary: The :future CSS pseudo-class selector is a time-dimensional pseudo-class that will match for any element which appears entirely after an element that matches :current.

entries.name: :has-slotted
entries.summary: The :has-slotted CSS pseudo-class matches when the content of a <slot> element is not empty or not using the default value (see Using templates and slots for more information).

entries.name: :has()
entries.summary: The functional :has() CSS pseudo-class represents an element if any of the relative selectors that are passed as an argument match at least one element when anchored against this element.

entries.name: :heading
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :host
entries.summary: The :host CSS pseudo-class selects the shadow host of the shadow DOM containing the CSS it is used inside — in other words, this allows you to select a custom element from inside its shadow DOM.

entries.name: :host-context()
entries.summary: Deprecated: This feature is no longer recommended.

entries.name: :hover
entries.summary: The :hover CSS pseudo-class matches an element when a user interacts with it using a pointing device.

entries.name: :in-range
entries.summary: The :in-range CSS pseudo-class represents an <input> element whose current value is within the range limits specified by the min and max attributes.

entries.name: :indeterminate
entries.summary: The :indeterminate CSS pseudo-class represents any form element whose state is indeterminate, such as checkboxes that have been set to an indeterminate state with JavaScript, radio buttons which are members of a group i…

entries.name: :interest-source
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :interest-target
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :invalid
entries.summary: The :invalid CSS pseudo-class represents any <form>, <fieldset>, <input> or other <form> element whose contents fail to validate.

entries.name: :is()
entries.summary: The :is() CSS pseudo-class function takes a selector list as its argument, and selects any element that can be selected by one of the selectors in that list.

entries.name: :lang()
entries.summary: The :lang() CSS pseudo-class matches elements based on the language they are determined to be in.

entries.name: :last-child
entries.summary: The :last-child CSS pseudo-class represents the last element among a group of sibling elements.

entries.name: :last-of-type
entries.summary: The :last-of-type CSS pseudo-class represents the last element of its type (tag name) among a group of sibling elements.

entries.name: :left
entries.summary: The :left CSS pseudo-class, used with the @page at-rule, represents all left-hand pages of a printed document.

entries.name: :link
entries.summary: The :link CSS pseudo-class represents an element that has not yet been visited. It matches every unvisited <a> or <area> element that has an href attribute.

entries.name: :local-link
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :modal
entries.summary: The :modal CSS pseudo-class matches an element that is in a state in which it excludes all interaction with elements outside it until the interaction has been dismissed.

entries.name: :muted
entries.summary: The :muted CSS pseudo-class selector represents an element that is capable of making sound, such as <audio> or <video>, but is muted (forced silent).

entries.name: :not()
entries.summary: The :not() CSS pseudo-class represents elements that do not match a list of selectors. Since it prevents specific items from being selected, it is known as the negation pseudo-class.

entries.name: :nth-child()
entries.summary: The :nth-child() CSS pseudo-class matches elements based on the indexes of the elements in the child list of their parents.

entries.name: :nth-last-child()
entries.summary: The :nth-last-child() CSS pseudo-class matches elements based on their position among a group of siblings, counting from the end.

entries.name: :nth-last-of-type()
entries.summary: The :nth-last-of-type() CSS pseudo-class matches elements based on their position among siblings of the same type (tag name), counting from the end.

entries.name: :nth-of-type()
entries.summary: The :nth-of-type() CSS pseudo-class matches elements based on their position among siblings of the same type (tag name).

entries.name: :only-child
entries.summary: The :only-child CSS pseudo-class represents an element without any siblings. This is the same as :first-child:last-child or :nth-child(1):nth-last-child(1), but with a lower specificity.

entries.name: :only-of-type
entries.summary: The :only-of-type CSS pseudo-class represents an element that has no siblings of the same type (tag name).

entries.name: :open
entries.summary: The :open CSS pseudo-class represents an element that has open and closed states, only when it is currently in the open state.

entries.name: :optional
entries.summary: The :optional CSS pseudo-class represents any <input>, <select>, or <textarea> element that does not have the required attribute set on it.

entries.name: :out-of-range
entries.summary: The :out-of-range CSS pseudo-class represents an <input> element whose current value is outside the range limits specified by the min and max attributes.

entries.name: :past
entries.summary: The :past CSS pseudo-class selector is a time-dimensional pseudo-class that will match for any element which appears entirely before an element that matches :current.

entries.name: :paused
entries.summary: The :paused CSS pseudo-class selector represents an element that is playable, such as <audio> or <video>, when that element is "paused" (i.e., not "playing").

entries.name: :picture-in-picture
entries.summary: The :picture-in-picture CSS pseudo-class matches the element which is currently in picture-in-picture mode.

entries.name: :placeholder-shown
entries.summary: The :placeholder-shown CSS pseudo-class represents any <input> or <textarea> element that is currently displaying placeholder text.

entries.name: :playing
entries.summary: The :playing CSS pseudo-class selector represents the playback state of an element that is playable, such as <audio> or <video>, when that element is "playing".

entries.name: :popover-open
entries.summary: The :popover-open CSS pseudo-class represents a popover element (i.e., one with a popover attribute) that is in the showing state. You can use this to apply style to popover elements only when they are shown.

entries.name: :read-only
entries.summary: The :read-only CSS pseudo-class selects elements (such as certain <input> types and <textarea>) that are not editable by the user.

entries.name: :read-write
entries.summary: The :read-write CSS pseudo-class represents an element (such as input or textarea) that is editable by the user.

entries.name: :required
entries.summary: The :required CSS pseudo-class represents any <input>, <select>, or <textarea> element that has the required attribute set on it.

entries.name: :right
entries.summary: The :right CSS pseudo-class, used with the @page at-rule, represents all right-hand pages of a printed document.

entries.name: :root
entries.summary: The :root CSS pseudo-class matches the root element of a tree representing the document.

entries.name: :scope
entries.summary: The :scope CSS pseudo-class represents elements that are a reference point, or scope, for selectors to match against.

entries.name: :seeking
entries.summary: The :seeking CSS pseudo-class selector represents an element that is playable, such as <audio> or <video>, when the playable element is seeking a playback position in the media resource.

entries.name: :stalled
entries.summary: The :stalled CSS pseudo-class selector represents an element that is playable, such as <audio> or <video>, when playback is stalled.

entries.name: :state()
entries.summary: The :state() CSS pseudo-class matches custom elements that have the specified custom state.

entries.name: :target
entries.summary: The :target CSS pseudo-class selects the target element of the document. When the document is loaded, the target element is derived using the document's URL fragment identifier.

entries.name: :target-after
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :target-before
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :target-current
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: :user-invalid
entries.summary: The :user-invalid CSS pseudo-class represents any validated form element whose value isn't valid based on their validation constraints, after the user has interacted with it.

entries.name: :user-valid
entries.summary: The :user-valid CSS pseudo-class represents any validated form element whose value validates correctly based on its validation constraints. However, unlike :valid it only matches once the user has interacted with it.

entries.name: :valid
entries.summary: The :valid CSS pseudo-class represents any <input> or other <form> element whose contents validate successfully.

entries.name: :visited
entries.summary: The :visited CSS pseudo-class applies once the link has been visited by the user. For privacy reasons, the styles that can be modified using this selector are very limited.

entries.name: :volume-locked
entries.summary: The :volume-locked CSS pseudo-class selector represents an element that is capable of making sound, such as <audio> or <video>, but the audio volume of the media element is currently "locked" by the user.

entries.name: :where()
entries.summary: The :where() CSS pseudo-class function takes a selector list as its argument, and selects any element that can be selected by one of the selectors in that list.

entries.name: :xr-overlay
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: @charset
entries.summary: The @charset CSS rule specifies the character encoding used in the style sheet. This syntax is useful when using non-ASCII characters in some CSS properties, like content.

entries.name: @color-profile
entries.summary: The @color-profile CSS at-rule defines and names a color profile which can later be used in the color() function to specify a color.

entries.name: @container
entries.summary: The @container CSS at-rule is a conditional group rule that applies styles to a containment context.

entries.name: @counter-style
entries.summary: The @counter-style CSS at-rule lets you extend predefined list styles and define your own counter styles that are not part of the predefined set of styles.

entries.name: @custom-media
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: @document
entries.summary: Deprecated: This feature is no longer recommended.

entries.name: @font-face
entries.summary: The @font-face CSS at-rule specifies a custom font with which to display text; the font can be loaded from either a remote server or a locally-installed font on the user's own computer.

entries.name: @font-feature-values
entries.summary: The @font-feature-values CSS at-rule lets you use a common name in the font-variant-alternates property for features activated differently in OpenType. This can help simplify your CSS when using multiple fonts.

entries.name: @font-palette-values
entries.summary: The @font-palette-values CSS at-rule allows you to customize the default values of font-palette created by the font-maker.

entries.name: @function
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: @import
entries.summary: The @import CSS at-rule is used to import style rules from other valid stylesheets.

entries.name: @keyframes
entries.summary: The @keyframes CSS at-rule controls the intermediate steps in a CSS animation sequence by defining styles for keyframes (or waypoints) along the animation sequence.

entries.name: @layer
entries.summary: The @layer CSS at-rule is used to declare a cascade layer and can also be used to define the order of precedence in case of multiple cascade layers.

entries.name: @media
entries.summary: The @media CSS at-rule can be used to apply part of a style sheet based on the result of one or more media queries.

entries.name: @namespace
entries.summary: @namespace is an at-rule that defines XML namespaces to be used in a CSS style sheet.

entries.name: @page
entries.summary: The @page at-rule is a CSS at-rule used to modify different aspects of printed pages. It targets and modifies the page's dimensions, orientation, and margins.

entries.name: @position-try
entries.summary: The @position-try CSS at-rule is used to define a custom position try fallback option, which can be used to define positioning and alignment for anchor-positioned elements.

entries.name: @property
entries.summary: The @property CSS at-rule is used to explicitly define CSS custom properties, allowing for property type checking and constraining, setting default values, and defining whether a custom property can inherit values or no…

entries.name: @scope
entries.summary: The @scope CSS at-rule enables you to select elements in specific DOM subtrees, targeting elements precisely without writing overly-specific selectors that are hard to override, and without coupling your selectors too t…

entries.name: @starting-style
entries.summary: The @starting-style CSS at-rule is used to define starting values for properties set on an element that you want to transition from when the element receives its first style update, i.e., when an element is first displa…

entries.name: @supports
entries.summary: The @supports CSS at-rule lets you specify CSS declarations that depend on a browser's support for CSS features. Using this at-rule is commonly called a feature query.

entries.name: @view-transition
entries.summary: The @view-transition CSS at-rule is used to opt in the current and destination documents to undergo a view transition, in the case of a cross-document navigation.

entries.name: abs()
entries.summary: The abs() CSS function returns the absolute value of the argument, as the same type as the input.

entries.name: accent-color
entries.summary: The accent-color CSS property sets the accent color for user-interface controls generated by some elements.

entries.name: acos()
entries.summary: The acos() CSS function is a trigonometric function that returns the inverse cosine of a number between -1 and 1. The function contains a single calculation that returns an <angle> between 0deg and 180deg.

entries.name: align-content
entries.summary: The CSS align-content property sets the distribution of space between and around content items along a flexbox's cross axis, or a grid or block-level element's block axis.

entries.name: cos()
entries.summary: The cos() CSS function is a trigonometric function that returns the cosine of a number, which is a value between -1 and 1.

entries.name: counter-increment
entries.summary: The counter-increment CSS property can be used to increase or decrease the value of the named CSS counters by the specified values, or to prevent all counters or an individual counter's value from being changed.

entries.name: counter-reset
entries.summary: The counter-reset CSS property creates named CSS counters and initializes them to a specific value.

entries.name: counter-set
entries.summary: The counter-set CSS property sets CSS counters on the element to the given values.

entries.name: counter()
entries.summary: The counter() CSS function returns a string representing the current value of the named counter, if there is one.

entries.name: counters()
entries.summary: The counters() CSS function enables combining markers when nesting counters.

entries.name: cross-fade()
entries.summary: The cross-fade() CSS function can be used to blend two or more images at a defined transparency.

entries.name: cubic-bezier()
entries.summary: The cubic-bezier() CSS function creates a smooth transition using a cubic Bézier curve. As an <easing-function>, it can be used to smooth out the start and end of the interpolation.

entries.name: cursor
entries.summary: The cursor CSS property sets the mouse cursor, if any, to show when the mouse pointer is over an element.

entries.name: cx
entries.summary: The cx CSS property defines the x-axis center point of an SVG <circle> or <ellipse> element. If present, it overrides the element's cx attribute.

entries.name: cy
entries.summary: The cy CSS property defines the y-axis center point of an SVG <circle> or <ellipse> elements. If present, it overrides the element's cy attribute.

entries.name: d
entries.summary: The d CSS property defines a path to be drawn by the SVG <path> element. If present, it overrides the element's d attribute.

entries.name: device-cmyk()
entries.summary: The device-cmyk() functional notation is used to express CMYK colors in a device dependent way, specifying the cyan, magenta, yellow, and black components.

entries.name: direction
entries.summary: Warning: Where possible, authors are encouraged to avoid using the direction CSS property and use the HTML dir global attribute instead.

entries.name: display
entries.summary: The display CSS property sets whether an element is treated as a block or inline box and the layout used for its children, such as flow layout, grid or flex.

entries.name: dominant-baseline
entries.summary: The dominant-baseline CSS property specifies the specific baseline used to align the box's text and inline-level contents.

entries.name: drop-shadow()
entries.summary: The drop-shadow() CSS function applies a drop shadow effect to the input image. Its result is a <filter-function>.

entries.name: dynamic-range-limit
entries.summary: The dynamic-range-limit CSS property specifies the maximum luminance allowed for High Dynamic Range (HDR) content.

entries.name: ellipse()
entries.summary: The ellipse() CSS function is one of the <basic-shape> data types.

entries.name: empty-cells
entries.summary: The empty-cells CSS property sets whether borders and backgrounds appear around <table> cells that have no visible content.

entries.name: env()
entries.summary: The env() CSS function can be used to insert the value of a user-agent defined environment variable into your CSS.

entries.name: exp()
entries.summary: The exp() CSS function is an exponential function that takes a number as an argument and returns the mathematical constant e raised to the power of the given number.

entries.name: field-sizing
entries.summary: The field-sizing CSS property enables you to control the sizing behavior of elements that are given a default preferred size, such as form control elements.

entries.name: fill
entries.summary: The fill CSS property defines how SVG text content and the interior canvas of SVG shapes are filled or painted. If present, it overrides the element's fill attribute.

entries.name: fill-opacity
entries.summary: The fill-opacity CSS property defines the opacity of the painting operation (color, gradient, pattern, etc.) applied to SVG shapes or text content elements to fill the element.

entries.name: fill-rule
entries.summary: The fill-rule CSS property defines the rule used to determine which parts of the SVG shape's canvas are included inside a shape to be filled. If present, it overrides the element's fill-rule attribute.

entries.name: filter
entries.summary: The filter CSS property applies graphical effects like blur or color shift to an element. Filters are commonly used to adjust the rendering of images, backgrounds, and borders.

entries.name: fit-content()
entries.summary: The fit-content() CSS function clamps a given size to an available size according to the formula min(maximum size, max(minimum size, argument)).

entries.name: flex
entries.summary: The flex CSS shorthand property sets how a flex item will grow or shrink to fit the space available in its flex container.

entries.name: flex-basis
entries.summary: The flex-basis CSS property sets the initial main size of a flex item. It sets the size of the content box unless otherwise set with box-sizing.

entries.name: flex-direction
entries.summary: The flex-direction CSS property sets how flex items are placed in the flex container defining the main axis and the direction (normal or reversed).

entries.name: flex-flow
entries.summary: The flex-flow CSS shorthand property specifies the direction of a flex container, as well as its wrapping behavior.

entries.name: flex-grow
entries.summary: The flex-grow CSS property sets the flex grow factor, which specifies how much of the flex container's positive free space, if any, should be assigned to the flex item's main size.

entries.name: flex-line-count
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: flex-shrink
entries.summary: The flex-shrink CSS property sets the flex shrink factor of a flex item. If the size of all flex items is larger than the flex container, the flex items can shrink to fit according to their flex-shrink value.

entries.name: flex-wrap
entries.summary: The flex-wrap CSS property sets whether flex items are forced onto one line or can wrap onto multiple lines. If wrapping is allowed, it sets the direction that lines are stacked.

entries.name: float
entries.summary: The float CSS property places an element on the left or right side of its container, allowing text and inline elements to wrap around it.

entries.name: flood-color
entries.summary: The flood-color CSS property defines the color of the current filter primitive subregion in <feFlood> and <feDropShadow> elements within a <filter>. If present, it overrides the element's flood-color attribute.

entries.name: flood-opacity
entries.summary: The flood-opacity CSS property defines the opacity of the current filter primitive subregion in <feFlood> and <feDropShadow> elements within a <filter>. If present, it overrides the element's flood-opacity attribute.

entries.name: font
entries.summary: The font CSS shorthand property sets all the different properties of an element's font. Alternatively, it sets an element's font to a system font.

entries.name: font-family
entries.summary: The font-family CSS property specifies a prioritized list of one or more font family names and/or generic family names for the selected element.

entries.name: font-feature-settings
entries.summary: The font-feature-settings CSS property controls advanced typographic features in OpenType fonts.

entries.name: font-kerning
entries.summary: The font-kerning CSS property sets the use of the kerning information stored in a font.

entries.name: font-language-override
entries.summary: The font-language-override CSS property controls the use of language-specific glyphs in a typeface.

entries.name: font-optical-sizing
entries.summary: The font-optical-sizing CSS property sets whether text rendering is optimized for viewing at different sizes.

entries.name: font-palette
entries.summary: The font-palette CSS property allows specifying one of the many palettes contained in a color font that a user agent may use for the font.

entries.name: font-size
entries.summary: The font-size CSS property sets the size of the font. Changing the font size also updates the sizes of the font size-relative <length> units, such as em, ex, and so forth.

entries.name: font-size-adjust
entries.summary: The font-size-adjust CSS property adjusts the size of a font to match a chosen font metric, such as the height of lowercase letters, to a specified proportion of the font-size.

entries.name: font-smooth
entries.summary: Non-standard: This feature is non-standard and is not on a standards track. Do not use it on production sites facing the Web: it will not work for every user.

entries.name: font-stretch
entries.summary: Note: The font-stretch property was renamed to font-width in the CSS Fonts specification. To preserve compatibility, the specification retains font-stretch as a legacy alias for the font-width property.

entries.name: font-style
entries.summary: The font-style CSS property sets whether a font should be styled with a normal, italic, or oblique face from its font-family.

entries.name: font-synthesis-small-caps
entries.summary: The font-synthesis-small-caps CSS property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize small-caps typeface when it is missing in a font family.

entries.name: font-synthesis-style
entries.summary: The font-synthesis-style CSS property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize the oblique typeface when it is missing in a font family.

entries.name: font-synthesis-weight
entries.summary: The font-synthesis-weight CSS property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize the bold typeface when it is missing in a font family.

entries.name: font-variant
entries.summary: The font-variant CSS shorthand property allows you to set all the font variants for a font.

entries.name: font-variant-alternates
entries.summary: The font-variant-alternates CSS property controls the usage of alternate glyphs. These alternate glyphs may be referenced by alternative names defined in @font-feature-values.

entries.name: font-variant-caps
entries.summary: The font-variant-caps CSS property controls the use of alternate glyphs used for small or petite capitals or for titling.

entries.name: font-variant-east-asian
entries.summary: The font-variant-east-asian CSS property controls the use of alternate glyphs for East Asian scripts, like Japanese and Chinese.

entries.name: font-variant-emoji
entries.summary: The font-variant-emoji CSS property specifies the default presentation style for displaying emojis.

entries.name: font-variant-ligatures
entries.summary: The font-variant-ligatures CSS property controls which ligatures and contextual forms are used in the textual content of the elements it applies to. This leads to more harmonized forms in the resulting text.

entries.name: font-variant-numeric
entries.summary: The font-variant-numeric CSS property controls the usage of alternate glyphs for numbers, fractions, and ordinal markers.

entries.name: font-variant-position
entries.summary: The font-variant-position CSS property controls the use of alternate, smaller glyphs that are positioned as superscript or subscript.

entries.name: font-variation-settings
entries.summary: The font-variation-settings CSS property provides low-level control over variable font characteristics by letting you specify the four letter axis names of the characteristics you want to vary along with their values.

entries.name: font-weight
entries.summary: The font-weight CSS property sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. The weights available depend on the font-family that is currently set.

entries.name: font-width
entries.summary: Note: The font-width property is the modern replacement for font-stretch, which is a legacy alias. While font-width is the specification's preferred name, font-stretch currently has broader browser support.

entries.name: forced-color-adjust
entries.summary: The forced-color-adjust CSS property allows authors to opt certain elements out of forced colors mode. This then restores the control of those values to CSS.

entries.name: frame-sizing
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: gap
entries.summary: The gap CSS shorthand property sets the gaps (also called gutters) between rows and columns on multi-column, flex, and grid containers.

entries.name: grayscale()
entries.summary: The grayscale() CSS function converts the input image to grayscale. Its result is a <filter-function>.

entries.name: grid
entries.summary: The grid CSS shorthand property sets all of the explicit and implicit grid properties in a single declaration.

entries.name: grid-area
entries.summary: The grid-area CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a grid by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the edges of its grid area.

entries.name: grid-auto-columns
entries.summary: The grid-auto-columns CSS property specifies the size of an implicitly-created grid column track or pattern of tracks.

entries.name: grid-auto-flow
entries.summary: The grid-auto-flow CSS property controls how the auto-placement algorithm works, specifying exactly how auto-placed items get flowed into the grid.

entries.name: grid-auto-rows
entries.summary: The grid-auto-rows CSS property specifies the size of an implicitly-created grid row track or pattern of tracks.

entries.summary: The grid-column-start CSS property specifies a grid item's start position within the grid column by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement.

entries.name: grid-template
entries.summary: The grid-template CSS shorthand property specifies the grid columns, grid rows, and grid areas.

entries.name: grid-template-areas
entries.summary: The grid-template-areas CSS property specifies named grid areas, establishing the cells in the grid and assigning them names.

entries.name: grid-template-columns
entries.summary: The grid-template-columns CSS property defines the line names and track sizing functions of the grid columns.

entries.name: grid-template-rows
entries.summary: The grid-template-rows CSS property defines the line names and track sizing functions of the grid rows.

entries.name: hanging-punctuation
entries.summary: The hanging-punctuation CSS property specifies whether a punctuation mark should hang at the start or end of a line of text. Hanging punctuation may be placed outside the line box.

entries.name: height
entries.summary: The height CSS property specifies the height of an element. By default, the property defines the height of the content area.

entries.name: hsl()
entries.summary: Note: The hsla() functional notation is an alias for hsl(). They are exactly equivalent. It is recommended to use hsl().

entries.name: hue-rotate()
entries.summary: The hue-rotate() CSS function rotates the hue of an element and its contents. Its result is a <filter-function>.

entries.name: hwb()
entries.summary: The hwb() functional notation expresses a color in the sRGB color space according to its hue, whiteness, and blackness. An optional alpha component represents the color's transparency.

entries.name: hyphenate-character
entries.summary: The hyphenate-character CSS property sets the character (or string) used at the end of a line before a hyphenation break.

entries.name: hyphenate-limit-chars
entries.summary: The hyphenate-limit-chars CSS property specifies the minimum word length to allow hyphenation of words as well as the minimum number of characters before and after the hyphen.

entries.name: hyphens
entries.summary: The hyphens CSS property specifies how words should be hyphenated when text wraps across multiple lines.

entries.name: hypot()
entries.summary: The hypot() CSS function is an exponential function that returns the square root of the sum of squares of its parameters.

entries.name: image-orientation
entries.summary: The image-orientation CSS property specifies a layout-independent correction to the orientation of an image.

entries.name: image-rendering
entries.summary: The image-rendering CSS property sets an image scaling algorithm. The property applies to an element itself, to any images set in its other properties, and to its descendants.

entries.name: image-resolution
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: image-set()
entries.summary: The image-set() CSS functional notation is a method of letting the browser pick the most appropriate CSS image from a given set, primarily for high pixel density screens.

entries.name: image()
entries.summary: The image() CSS function defines an <image> in a similar fashion to the url() function, but with added functionality including specifying the image's directionality, displaying just a part of that image defined by a med…

entries.name: initial-letter
entries.summary: The initial-letter CSS property sets the size and sink for dropped, raised, and sunken initial letters. This property applies to ::first-letter pseudo-elements and inline-level first children of block containers.

entries.name: inline-size
entries.summary: The inline-size CSS property defines the size of an element's block along the inline axis. If the writing-mode is horizontal, it corresponds to the width; if the writing mode is vertical, it corresponds to the height.

entries.name: inset
entries.summary: The inset CSS shorthand property corresponds to the top, right, bottom, and/or left properties. It has the same multi-value syntax of the margin shorthand.

entries.name: inset-block
entries.summary: The inset-block CSS shorthand property defines the logical block start and end offsets of an element, which maps to physical offsets depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: inset-block-end
entries.summary: The inset-block-end CSS property defines the logical block end offset of an element, which maps to a physical inset depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: inset-block-start
entries.summary: The inset-block-start CSS property defines the logical block start offset of an element, which maps to a physical inset depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: inset-inline-end
entries.summary: The inset-inline-end CSS property defines the logical inline end inset of an element, which maps to a physical offset depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: inset-inline-start
entries.summary: The inset-inline-start CSS property defines the logical inline start inset of an element, which maps to a physical offset depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: inset()
entries.summary: The inset() CSS function defines a rectangle at the specified inset distances from each side of the reference box. It is a basic shape function used to define one of the <basic-shape> data types.

entries.name: interactivity

entries.name: interpolate-size

entries.name: invert()
entries.summary: The invert() CSS function inverts the color samples in the input image. Its result is a <filter-function>.

entries.name: isolation
entries.summary: The isolation CSS property determines whether an element must create a new stacking context.

entries.name: justify-content
entries.summary: The CSS justify-content property defines how the browser distributes space between and around content items along the main axis of a flex container and the inline axis of grid and multicol containers.

entries.name: justify-items
entries.summary: The CSS justify-items property defines the default justify-self for all items of the box, giving them all a default way of justifying each box along the appropriate axis.

entries.name: justify-self
entries.summary: The CSS justify-self property sets the way a box is justified inside its alignment container along the appropriate axis.

entries.name: lab()
entries.summary: The lab() functional notation expresses a given color in the CIE L*a*b* color space.

entries.name: layer()
entries.summary: The layer() CSS function is used along with the @import at-rule to put the imported resource in a separate named cascade layer.

entries.name: lch()
entries.summary: The lch() functional notation expresses a given color using the LCH color space, which represents lightness, chroma, and hue.

entries.name: left
entries.summary: The left CSS property participates in specifying the horizontal position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.

entries.name: letter-spacing
entries.summary: The letter-spacing CSS property sets the spacing between text characters. This value is added to the natural spacing between characters while rendering the text.

entries.name: light-dark()
entries.summary: The light-dark() CSS function accepts two colors or two images and returns a color or an image based on the active color scheme, without needing a prefers-color-scheme media feature.

entries.name: lighting-color
entries.summary: The lighting-color CSS property defines the color of the light source for the <feDiffuseLighting> and <feSpecularLighting> SVG lighting filter primitives within an SVG <filter>.

entries.name: line-break
entries.summary: The line-break CSS property sets how to break lines of Chinese, Japanese, or Korean (CJK) text when working with punctuation and symbols.

entries.name: line-clamp
entries.summary: The line-clamp CSS property allows limiting of the contents of a block to the specified number of lines. Optionally, it also allows inserting content into the last line to indicate that content was truncated.

entries.name: line-height
entries.summary: The line-height CSS property sets the height of a line box in horizontal writing modes. In vertical writing modes, it sets the width of a line box. It's commonly used to set the distance between lines of text.

entries.name: line-height-step
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: linear-gradient()
entries.summary: The linear-gradient() CSS function creates an image consisting of a progressive transition between two or more colors along a straight line.

entries.name: linear()
entries.summary: The linear() CSS function creates a transition curve that progresses uniformly between points. As an <easing-function>, it creates transitions where the interpolation occurs at a constant rate from beginning to end.

entries.name: link-parameters
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: list-style
entries.summary: The list-style CSS shorthand property allows you to set all the list style properties at once.

entries.name: list-style-image
entries.summary: The list-style-image CSS property sets an image to be used as the list item marker.

entries.name: list-style-position
entries.summary: The list-style-position CSS property sets the position of the ::marker relative to a list item.

entries.name: list-style-type
entries.summary: The list-style-type CSS property sets the marker (such as a disc, character, or custom counter style) of a list item element.

entries.name: log()
entries.summary: The log() CSS function is an exponential function that returns the logarithm of a number.

entries.name: margin
entries.summary: The margin CSS shorthand property sets the margin area on all four sides of an element.

entries.name: margin-block
entries.summary: The margin-block CSS shorthand property defines the logical block start and end margins of an element, which maps to physical margins depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: margin-block-end
entries.summary: The margin-block-end CSS property defines the logical block end margin of an element, which maps to a physical margin depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: margin-block-start
entries.summary: The margin-block-start CSS property defines the logical block start margin of an element, which maps to a physical margin depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: margin-bottom
entries.summary: The margin-bottom CSS property sets the margin area on the bottom of an element. A positive value places it farther from its neighbors, while a negative value places it closer.

entries.name: margin-inline
entries.summary: The margin-inline CSS shorthand property defines both the logical inline start and end margins of an element, which maps to physical margins depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: margin-inline-end
entries.summary: The margin-inline-end CSS property defines the logical inline end margin of an element, which maps to a physical margin depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: margin-inline-start
entries.summary: The margin-inline-start CSS property defines the logical inline start margin of an element, which maps to a physical margin depending on the element's writing mode, directionality, and text orientation.

entries.name: margin-left
entries.summary: The margin-left CSS property sets the margin area on the left side of an element. A positive value places it farther from its neighbors, while a negative value places it closer.

entries.name: margin-right
entries.summary: The margin-right CSS property sets the margin area on the right side of an element. A positive value places it farther from its neighbors, while a negative value places it closer.

entries.name: margin-top
entries.summary: The margin-top CSS property sets the margin area on the top of an element. A positive value places it farther from its neighbors, while a negative value places it closer.

entries.name: margin-trim
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: marker
entries.summary: The marker CSS property points to a marker that will be drawn on the first, middle, and last vertices of the element's path; that is, at all of its vertices.

entries.name: marker-end
entries.summary: The marker-end CSS property points to a marker that will be drawn on the last vertex of the element's path; that is, at its ending vertex.

entries.name: marker-mid
entries.summary: The marker-mid CSS property points to a marker that will be drawn on the middle vertices of the element's path; that is, at each of its vertices between the start and end vertices.

entries.name: marker-start
entries.summary: The marker-start CSS property points to a marker that will be drawn on the first vertex of the element's path; that is, at its starting vertex.

entries.name: mask
entries.summary: The mask CSS shorthand property hides an element (partially or fully) by masking or clipping a specified area of the image. It is a shorthand for all the mask-* properties.

entries.name: mask-border
entries.summary: The mask-border CSS shorthand property lets you create a mask along the edge of an element's border.

entries.name: mask-border-mode
entries.summary: The mask-border-mode CSS property specifies the blending mode used in a mask border.

entries.name: mask-border-outset
entries.summary: The mask-border-outset CSS property specifies the distance by which an element's mask border is set out from its border box.

entries.name: mask-border-repeat
entries.summary: The mask-border-repeat CSS property specifies how the images for the sides and the middle part of the mask border image are scaled and tiled.

entries.name: mask-border-slice
entries.summary: The mask-border-slice CSS property divides the image set by mask-border-source into regions. These regions are used to form the components of an element's mask border.

entries.name: mask-border-source
entries.summary: The mask-border-source CSS property sets the source image used to create an element's mask border.

entries.name: mask-border-width
entries.summary: The mask-border-width CSS property sets the width of an element's mask border.

entries.name: mask-clip
entries.summary: The mask-clip CSS property determines the area which is affected by a mask. The painted content of an element must be restricted to this area.

entries.name: mask-composite

entries.summary: The sibling-index() CSS function returns an integer representing the position of the current element in the DOM tree relative to all its sibling elements.

entries.name: sign()
entries.summary: The sign() CSS function contains one calculation, and returns -1 if the numeric value of the argument is negative, +1 if the numeric value of the argument is positive, 0⁺ if the numeric value of the argument is 0⁺, and…

entries.name: sin()
entries.summary: The sin() CSS function is a trigonometric function that returns the sine of a number, which is a value between -1 and 1.

entries.name: skew()
entries.summary: The skew() CSS function defines a transformation that skews an element on the 2D plane. Its result is a <transform-function> data type.

entries.name: speak-as
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: sqrt()
entries.summary: The sqrt() CSS function is an exponential function that returns the square root of a number.

entries.name: steps()
entries.summary: The steps() CSS function defines a transition that divides the input time into a specified number of intervals that are equal in length. This subclass of step functions are sometimes also called staircase functions.

entries.name: stop-color
entries.summary: The stop-color CSS property defines the color to use for an SVG <stop> element within a gradient. If present, it overrides the element's stop-color attribute.

entries.name: stop-opacity
entries.summary: The stop-opacity CSS property defines the opacity of a given color gradient stop in the SVG <stop> element within an SVG gradient. If present, it overrides the element's stop-opacity attribute.

entries.name: stroke
entries.summary: The stroke CSS property defines the color or SVG paint server used to draw an element's stroke.

entries.name: stroke-dasharray
entries.summary: The stroke-dasharray CSS property defines a pattern of dashes and gaps used in the painting of the SVG shape's stroke. If present, it overrides the element's stroke-dasharray attribute.

entries.name: stroke-dashoffset
entries.summary: The stroke-dashoffset CSS property defines an offset for the starting point of the rendering of an SVG element's associated dash array. If present, it overrides the element's stroke-dashoffset attribute.

entries.name: stroke-linecap
entries.summary: The stroke-linecap CSS property defines the shape to be used at the end of open subpaths of SVG elements' unclosed strokes. If present, it overrides the element's stroke-linecap attribute.

entries.name: stroke-linejoin
entries.summary: The stroke-linejoin CSS property defines the shape to be used at the corners of an SVG element's stroked paths. If present, it overrides the element's stroke-linejoin attribute.

entries.name: stroke-miterlimit
entries.summary: The stroke-miterlimit CSS property defines a limit on the ratio of the miter length to the stroke-width when the shape to be used at the corners of an SVG element's stroked path is a mitered join.

entries.name: stroke-opacity
entries.summary: The stroke-opacity CSS property defines the opacity of an SVG shape's stroke. The effect is identical to that of opacity, except it is applied only to the stroke, not to the entire element.

entries.name: stroke-width
entries.summary: The stroke-width CSS property defines the width of a stroke applied to the SVG shape. If present, it overrides the element's stroke-width attribute.

entries.name: superellipse()
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: symbols()
entries.summary: The symbols() CSS function enables defining counter styles inline, directly as a value of properties such as list-style, providing a less powerful but simpler alternative to the @counter-style method of defining a count…

entries.name: tab-size
entries.summary: The tab-size CSS property is used to customize the width of tab characters (U+0009).

entries.name: table-layout
entries.summary: The table-layout CSS property sets the algorithm used to lay out <table> cells, rows, and columns.

entries.name: tan()
entries.summary: The tan() CSS function is a trigonometric function that returns the tangent of a number, which is a value between −infinity and infinity.

entries.name: text-align
entries.summary: The text-align CSS property sets the horizontal alignment of the inline-level content inside a block element or table-cell box. This means it works like vertical-align but in the horizontal direction.

entries.name: text-align-last
entries.summary: The text-align-last CSS property sets how the last line of a block or a line, right before a forced line break, is aligned.

entries.name: text-anchor
entries.summary: The text-anchor CSS property aligns a box containing a string of text where the wrapping area is determined from the inline-size property, and the text is then placed relative to the anchor point of the element, which i…

entries.name: text-autospace
entries.summary: The text-autospace CSS property allows you to specify the space applied between Chinese/Japanese/Korean (CJK) and non-CJK characters.

entries.name: text-box
entries.summary: The text-box CSS shorthand property corresponds to the text-box-trim and text-box-edge properties, which together specify the amount of space to trim from the block-start edge and block-end edge of a text element's bloc…

entries.name: text-box-edge
entries.summary: The text-box-edge CSS property specifies an amount of space to trim from a text element's block container.

entries.name: text-box-trim
entries.summary: The text-box-trim CSS property specifies which of the over and under edges of text content to trim from a text element's block container.

entries.name: text-combine-upright
entries.summary: The text-combine-upright CSS property sets the combination of characters into the space of a single character. If the combined text is wider than 1em, the user agent must fit the contents within 1em.

entries.name: text-decoration
entries.summary: The text-decoration CSS shorthand property sets the appearance of decorative lines on text.

entries.name: text-decoration-color
entries.summary: The text-decoration-color CSS property sets the color of decorations added to text by text-decoration-line.

entries.name: text-decoration-inset
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: text-decoration-line
entries.summary: The text-decoration-line CSS property sets the kind of decoration that is used on text in an element, such as an underline or overline.

entries.name: text-decoration-skip
entries.summary: Deprecated: This feature is no longer recommended.

entries.name: text-decoration-skip-ink
entries.summary: The text-decoration-skip-ink CSS property specifies how overlines and underlines are drawn when they pass over glyph ascenders and descenders.

entries.name: text-decoration-style
entries.summary: The text-decoration-style CSS property sets the style of the lines specified by text-decoration-line. The style applies to all lines that are set with text-decoration-line.

entries.name: text-decoration-thickness
entries.summary: The text-decoration-thickness CSS property sets the stroke thickness of the decoration line that is used on text in an element, such as a line-through, underline, or overline.

entries.name: text-emphasis
entries.summary: The text-emphasis CSS shorthand property applies emphasis marks to text (except spaces and control characters).

entries.name: text-emphasis-color
entries.summary: The text-emphasis-color CSS property sets the color of emphasis marks. This value can also be set using the text-emphasis shorthand.

entries.name: text-emphasis-position
entries.summary: The text-emphasis-position CSS property sets where emphasis marks are drawn. Similar to the text rendered by the <ruby> HTML element, if there isn't enough room for emphasis marks, the line height is increased.

entries.name: text-emphasis-style
entries.summary: The text-emphasis-style CSS property sets the appearance of emphasis marks. It can also be set, and reset, using the text-emphasis shorthand.

entries.name: text-indent
entries.summary: The text-indent CSS property sets the length of empty space (indentation) that is put before lines of text in a block.

entries.name: text-justify
entries.summary: The text-justify CSS property sets what type of justification should be applied to text when text-align: justify; is set on an element.

entries.name: text-orientation
entries.summary: The text-orientation CSS property sets the orientation of the text characters in a line. It only affects text in vertical mode (when writing-mode is not horizontal-tb).

entries.name: text-overflow
entries.summary: The text-overflow CSS property sets how hidden overflow content is signaled to users.

entries.name: text-rendering
entries.summary: The text-rendering CSS property provides information to the rendering engine about what to optimize for when rendering text.

entries.name: text-shadow
entries.summary: The text-shadow CSS property adds shadows to text. It accepts a comma-separated list of shadows to be applied to the text and any of its text-decoration.

entries.name: text-size-adjust
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: text-spacing-trim
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: text-transform
entries.summary: The text-transform CSS property specifies how to capitalize an element's text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized.

entries.name: text-underline-offset
entries.summary: The text-underline-offset CSS property sets the offset distance of an underline text decoration line (applied using text-decoration) from its original position.

entries.name: text-underline-position
entries.summary: The text-underline-position CSS property specifies the position of the underline which is set using the text-decoration property's underline value.

entries.name: text-wrap
entries.summary: The text-wrap CSS shorthand property controls how text inside an element is wrapped. The different values provide:

entries.name: text-wrap-mode
entries.summary: The text-wrap-mode CSS property controls whether the text inside an element is wrapped.

entries.name: text-wrap-style
entries.summary: The text-wrap-style CSS property controls how text inside an element is wrapped, providing alternate ways of determining where to create line breaks in order to fit the content within a block element.

entries.name: timeline-scope
entries.summary: The timeline-scope CSS property modifies the scope of a named animation timeline.

entries.name: top
entries.summary: The top CSS property sets the vertical position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.

entries.name: touch-action
entries.summary: The touch-action CSS property sets how an element's region can be manipulated by a touchscreen user (for example, by zooming features built into the browser).

entries.name: transform
entries.summary: The transform CSS property lets you rotate, scale, skew, or translate an element. It modifies the coordinate space of the CSS visual formatting model.

entries.name: transform-box
entries.summary: The transform-box CSS property defines the layout box to which the transform, individual transform properties translate, scale, and rotate, and transform-origin properties relate.

entries.name: transform-origin
entries.summary: The transform-origin CSS property sets the origin for an element's transformations.

entries.name: transform-style
entries.summary: The transform-style CSS property sets whether children of an element are positioned in the 3D space or are flattened in the plane of the element.

entries.name: transition
entries.summary: The transition CSS shorthand property for transition-property, transition-duration, transition-timing-function, transition-delay, and transition-behavior.

entries.name: transition-behavior
entries.summary: The transition-behavior CSS property specifies whether transitions will be started for properties whose animation behavior is discrete.

entries.name: transition-delay
entries.summary: The transition-delay CSS property specifies the duration to wait before starting a property's transition effect when its value changes.

entries.name: transition-duration
entries.summary: The transition-duration CSS property sets the length of time a transition animation should take to complete. By default, the value is 0s, meaning that no animation will occur.

entries.name: transition-property
entries.summary: The transition-property CSS property sets the CSS properties to which a transition effect should be applied.

entries.name: transition-timing-function
entries.summary: The transition-timing-function CSS property sets how intermediate values are calculated for CSS properties being affected by a transition effect.

entries.name: translate
entries.summary: The translate CSS property allows you to specify translation transforms individually and independently of the transform property.

entries.name: translate()
entries.summary: The translate() CSS function repositions an element in the horizontal and/or vertical directions. Its result is a <transform-function> data type.

entries.name: type()
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: unicode-bidi
entries.summary: The unicode-bidi CSS property, together with the direction property, determines how bidirectional text in a document is handled.

entries.name: url()
entries.summary: The url() CSS function is used to include a file. The parameter is an absolute URL, a relative URL, a blob URL, or a data URL.

entries.name: user-modify
entries.summary: Deprecated: This feature is no longer recommended.

entries.name: user-select
entries.summary: The user-select CSS property controls whether the user can select text. This doesn't have any effect on content loaded as part of a browser's user interface (its chrome), except in textboxes.

entries.name: var()
entries.summary: The var() CSS function can be used to insert the value of a custom property (sometimes called a "CSS variable") instead of any part of a value of another property.

entries.name: vector-effect
entries.summary: The vector-effect CSS property suppresses specific transformation effects in SVG, thus permitting effects like a road on a map staying the same width no matter how the map is zoomed, or allowing a diagram key to retain…

entries.name: vertical-align
entries.summary: The vertical-align CSS shorthand property sets the vertical alignment of an inline, inline-block, or table-cell box.

entries.name: view-timeline
entries.summary: The view-timeline CSS shorthand property defines a named view progress timeline's name, direction, and inset values.

entries.name: view-timeline-axis
entries.summary: The view-timeline-axis CSS property specifies the scroll direction to be used for a named view progress timeline.

entries.name: view-timeline-inset
entries.summary: The view-timeline-inset CSS property is used to specify one or two values representing an adjustment to the position of the scrollport (see Scroll container for more details) in which the subject element of a named view…

entries.name: view-timeline-name
entries.summary: The view-timeline-name CSS property specifies the names of one or more named view progress timelines associated with the element.

entries.name: view-transition-class
entries.summary: The view-transition-class CSS property provides the selected elements with one or more identifying classes (<custom-ident>s), providing an additional method of styling the view transitions for those elements.

entries.name: view-transition-name
entries.summary: The view-transition-name CSS property specifies the view transition snapshot that selected elements will participate in.

entries.name: view-transition-scope
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: view()
entries.summary: The view() CSS function is used with the animation-timeline property to create an anonymous view progress timeline based on when an element comes into view inside its nearest scroll container.

entries.name: visibility
entries.summary: The visibility CSS property shows or hides an element without changing the layout of a document. The property can also hide rows or columns in a <table>.

entries.name: white-space
entries.summary: The white-space CSS shorthand property sets how white space inside an element is handled.

entries.name: white-space-collapse
entries.summary: The white-space-collapse CSS property controls how white space inside an element is collapsed.

entries.name: widows
entries.summary: The widows CSS property sets the minimum number of lines in a block container that must be shown at the top of a page, region, or column.

entries.name: width
entries.summary: The width CSS property sets an element's width. By default, it sets the width of the content area, but if box-sizing is set to border-box, it sets the width of the border area.

entries.name: will-change
entries.summary: The will-change CSS property enables optimizing animations by providing a rendering hint to a browser about how an element is expected to change.

entries.name: word-break
entries.summary: The word-break CSS property sets whether line breaks appear wherever the text would otherwise overflow its content box.

entries.name: word-spacing
entries.summary: The word-spacing CSS property sets the spacing between words and between tags.

entries.name: writing-mode
entries.summary: The writing-mode CSS property sets whether lines of text are laid out horizontally or vertically, as well as the direction in which text flows.

entries.name: x
entries.summary: The x CSS property defines the x-axis coordinate of the top left corner of the SVG <rect> shape, <image> image, <foreignObject> viewport or nested <svg> viewport relative to the nearest <svg> ancestor's user coordinate…

entries.name: xywh()
entries.summary: The xywh() CSS function creates a rectangle using the specified distances from the left (x) and top (y) edges of the containing block and the specified width (w) and height (h) of the rectangle.

entries.name: y
entries.summary: The y CSS property defines the y-axis coordinate of the top left corner of the SVG <rect> shape, <image> image, <foreignObject> viewport and nested <svg> viewport relative to the nearest <svg> ancestor's user coordinate…

entries.name: z-index
entries.summary: The z-index CSS property sets the z-order of a positioned element and its descendants or flex and grid items. Overlapping elements with a larger z-index cover those with a smaller one.

entries.name: zoom
entries.summary: The zoom CSS property can be used to control the magnification level of an element. transform: scale() can be used as an alternative to this property.
